display.text: Treating p̂ as approximately normal with mean p and standard deviation √[p(1 − p)/n]. The course requires both np ≥ 10 and n(1 − p) ≥ 10.
The probability distribution of a statistic across repeated random samples of the same size from the same population.
The spread of p̂ across random samples of size n: √[p(1 − p)/n] for independent Bernoulli observations. This is the proportion's standard error.

response.correctResponse: standard deviation of the sample proportion

display.text: The standard deviation of the sampling distribution of x̄. For n independent observations with population standard deviation σ, it is σ/√n.
A sample mean's distance from μ in standard-error units: z = (x̄ − μ)/(σ/√n). Normal probabilities apply when the sampling distribution is normal or adequately approximated by it.
A sample proportion's distance from p in standard-error units: z = (p̂ − p)/√[p(1 − p)/n].
